name: Security Headers Checker
title: Security Headers: Check & Grade Any Site A–F
description: Free security headers checker: scan a URL for HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and more, graded A–F with copy-paste fixes.
answer: Security headers are HTTP response headers that tell browsers to enforce HTTPS, limit which scripts run and block clickjacking. Enter a URL to check HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, get an A–F grade and copy a starting configuration.
trust: We request the URL live and grade the headers your server actually returns; nothing is probed or attacked.
body:
## Security Headers Checker: The 6 Headers That Matter

Six headers do most of the work. Each one closes a specific door:

| Header | Protects against | Docs |
|---|---|---|
| Strict-Transport-Security | Downgrades to insecure HTTP | [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Strict-Transport-Security) |
| Content-Security-Policy | Cross-site scripting, injected scripts | [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CSP) |
| X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors | Clickjacking in hidden frames | [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Frame-Options) |
| X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff | Browsers guessing file types | [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Content-Type-Options) |
| Referrer-Policy | Leaking full URLs to other sites | [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Referrer-Policy) |
| Permissions-Policy | Unwanted camera, mic, location access | — |

## Security Headers Check: CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options

These three carry the most weight in the grade. HSTS and clickjacking protection are quick wins; CSP is the hardest, because a strict policy can break scripts. Start with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` to see violations without blocking anything, then tighten.

## How do real sites score?

Unevenly. In our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)):

- 84.1% sent HSTS, 72.7% had clickjacking protection and 62.2% sent nosniff;
- only 53.7% had a Content-Security-Policy, 37.1% a Referrer-Policy and 15.9% a Permissions-Policy;
- just 21.9% had all five of the core headers, and 6% had none of them.

## Do security headers help SEO?

Not directly as ranking signals, apart from HTTPS itself, which Google has used as a [lightweight ranking signal since 2014](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2014/08/https-as-ranking-signal). Their value is protecting visitors and your domain's reputation — a hijacked or defaced site loses rankings fast.

## How is the grade calculated?

Points for each header that's present and sensible, deductions for weak values such as a short HSTS max-age or `unsafe-url` referrer policy. A is 90 or more, F is under 35. The nginx snippet is a starting point: test it on staging, especially the CSP.

For HSTS specifically — max-age, subdomains and preload eligibility — use the [HSTS checker](/tools/hsts-checker). To see every header your server sends, use the [HTTP header checker](/tools/http-header-checker).

faqs.q: Which security headers should every website have?
faqs.a: At minimum Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, clickjacking protection with X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, a Referrer-Policy, and a Content-Security-Policy suited to your scripts.

faqs.q: Will adding a Content-Security-Policy break my site?
faqs.a: A strict CSP can block scripts, styles or embeds you rely on. Deploy it first as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, fix the reported violations, then enforce it.
No. Modern browsers have removed the XSS filter it controlled, so the header does nothing useful today. A Content-Security-Policy is the real protection.
